subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What public OpenClaw contract should represent outgoing Telegram custom emoji: raw Telegram HTML only, first-class message-tool/entity data, shared Markdown IR, or a Telegram-specific channelData shape?
rationale: The remaining gap crosses a user-facing tool schema and Telegram-owned delivery semantics; automation should not invent a plugin/API contract that maintainers may have to support long term.

options.title: Adopt a first-class entity contract
options.body: Add a validated custom emoji representation through the message tool or Telegram-owned channelData and wire it to `entities`/`caption_entities` while preserving current HTML fallback behavior.

options.title: Narrow to raw HTML passthrough
options.body: Document and test `<tg-emoji emoji-id="...">` as the supported path, and explicitly leave entity-array support out of scope for now.

options.title: Defer behind parse-mode work
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/10944 settle the broader Telegram formatting mode before adding any custom emoji-specific public surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt a first-class entity contract
recommendation.body: Add a validated custom emoji representation through the message tool or Telegram-owned channelData and wire it to `entities`/`caption_entities` while preserving current HTML fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This issue already has a steipete-authored maintainer/Codex comment calling for API-shape judgment across the same surfaces.
